summary: Self-hosted AI gateway that puts many model providers behind one API, with routing, access control, usage tracking and a web console.

heroCommands.command:
mkdir -p data
docker run --name new-api -d --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 -v "$(pwd)/data:/data" calciumion/new-api:latest

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: New API is a self-hosted AI gateway. You connect your upstream model services, and it gives your apps and team one consistent API, with routing, access control, usage tracking and cost accounting managed from a web console.
sixtySeconds.problem: Teams using several AI providers end up configuring keys and endpoints in every client and lose track of usage and cost. New API centralises that so you can switch providers without reconfiguring clients.
whoFor: Companies running a private multi-model service
Developers who switch between AI providers
Admins who need usage and cost tracking
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a self-hosted gateway with a web console, usage dashboards and model routing that you run on your own server.
requirements: Your own lawfully obtained upstream API keys

overview: The quickest start is a single Docker container with SQLite, bound to localhost; open http://localhost:3000 and complete the setup wizard to create the admin account. For production, the Docker Compose file starts New API with PostgreSQL and Redis.

Before using Compose, replace the example database and Redis passwords and set a persistent random SESSION_SECRET. The README stresses that it is for lawful, authorised use: you must obtain upstream keys legitimately and follow providers' terms, and public or resale services need the required filings and licences.
New API is licensed under AGPL-3.0.

steps.title: Start a single instance with SQLite
steps.code:
mkdir -p data
docker run --name new-api -d --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  -v "$(pwd)/data:/data" \
  calciumion/new-api:latest

steps.title: Finish setup
steps.body: Open http://localhost:3000 and complete the wizard to create the admin account.

steps.title: Edit docker-compose.yml
steps.body: Replace the example database and Redis passwords and set a persistent random SESSION_SECRET.

steps.title: Start it
steps.code:
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f new-api

environment.name: SESSION_SECRET
environment.description: Persistent random secret for sessions in Compose deployments.
